title: Jimmy Wade and the Isabella record with Francois Luzan
summary: Punch recalls the Wade band, the Isabella record and drummer Francois's club singing of a greasy pole song.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Who was in Jimmy Wade's band?
Well, Jimmy Wade had some fellas, no you asked me that once before Dick, but I swear I can't remember them fellas. I can't remember.
Maybe they just come back to you in the meantime.
Yeah, but he had a nice little old band.
Did you ever make any records with Jimmy Bertrand?
No. I knew them real good though.
Well who did you make Isabella with?

That was a little kid. He's a good drummer but he never had no idea about, you know, running no band. But he didn't put the band in his name, but he's a real good little drummer. He's on the order of this Paul Barbarian, Paul Barbarian. He just like him. Well who, uh... Who did run that band? Put that down, Lionel.
Who did run that band? What band?
Uh, Francois. Francois. Yeah. He ran it himself?

He managed? Well no, we all, you know, that's what somebody said went, you know. Yeah. Now this Francois had a pint, he'd wait with us in the Golden Lily, but he didn't, uh, he didn't do any bad. When I made a record with him, something about, some kind of blues he sung, I forgot. You got the weather. Huh?

That's right, that's it. Yeah, that's it. He had a song he used to sing. You know, you could go around them tables then, and the club, and sing anything to them people that liked it, you know. Boy, he had a song there about the greasy pole. Boy, I'm telling you, that track, I had to probably was a killer. The people used to love to hear him sing that greasy pole.
Well how did that song go?
Something about, uh, a man get tired of the same hole, and a woman get tired of the same greasy pole. You know, he had it all messed up there, some kind of way.
